reviews.text: A brainy bruiser that offers plenty of social commentary to go along with the exciting action.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Snowpiercer holds a violent thrill, a stomach plummet, and a soul-crashing revelation behind each new compartment door.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is a mix of something unfathomable, subversive, thought-provoking and thrilling.
reviews.author: Diana Tuova

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is one of the most unique post-apocalyptic film’s I’ve ever seen, and my pick for the best science fiction film from 2014.
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: ... a high-speed metaphor speeding down the science fiction tracks of genre cinema.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is one of the best films of the respective decade. With a brilliant screenplay, Bong Joon-ho delivers an extremely complex narrative, filled with emotionally shocking character development, and featuring excellent stunt work.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Bong Joon-ho’s first English-language film is this incredible world about class, global warming, and the price of freedom.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: The film's strength lies in the way the screenplay's built. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José C. Donayre Guerrero

reviews.text: This graphic novel adaptation is a blend of science fiction and social commentary that plays out like a video game... With it comes Chris Evans’ finest performance.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: It’s a visual delight.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Thoughtful, provocative, and far more enjoyable than your average blockbuster, Snowpiercer's pure entertainment value is outmatched only by its sobering commentary on the continual inhumanity of the human race.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: If you needed any more convincing of Bongs versatility as a director, credit should be given to the fact that this is an English-language film from a Korean director, that uses language and cultural perspective as a tool in the movies very storytelling.
reviews.author: Daisy Leigh-Phippard

reviews.text: Snowpiercer examines a class system that refuses to die no matter the circumstances. Director Bong Joon-ho constantly asks whether a person must accept their preordained place in society for the sake of balance and harmony.
reviews.author: Robert Sims

reviews.text: Part allegory, part Hero's Journey, Snowpiercer makes no concessions about its religious and political metaphors, and it is all the stronger for it.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Its satire of actual class warfare is as cutting as the axes the rebels and guards use.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: An extraordinary work of climate-change fiction, with bold visuals, gripping action, shocking violence and a brutally clear allegory for the class system.
reviews.author: George Fenwick

reviews.text: It's just as interested in examining topics like climate change, class, and cultural disparity as it is in revealing just how the film's core team navigates a never-stopping hell train to take on the bad guys.
reviews.author: Nathan Mattise

reviews.text: An environmental thriller - if you haven't already seen Bong's "The Host" do so now! - that is unapologetically weird, keeping the audience off balance for the entirety of its two-hour running time.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Overflows with ideas, encompassing the spectrum from vividly bizarre to profoundly mesmerizing.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Insanely brilliant.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: It has plenty of action, while the story contains an unexpected intelligence. It has a message, but never gets too preachy. It's very violent, yet avoids being overly bloody. It's dark, but knows when to lighten the mood.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Bleak and grim and almost desolate, there is a spark of hope, just enough to keep the gloom and doom from becoming oppressive.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: [It] holds great promise yet never finds its track.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: A riveting mix of disturbing drama and edgy action, seasoned with sharp wit.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: I wouldn't really recommend it.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: An electrifying, horrifying and witty study of society and class wrapped up in a sci-fi action movie.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: It's a hot mess.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: ...an extremely visceral experience, with much to say about contemporary western society. We couldn't expect anything less from Bong. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: It is a big, complex, bloody, noisy and quite sophisticated motion picture. It was meant to be seen on a large screen with surround-sound rumbling and roaring around you.
reviews.author: Kathi Maio

reviews.text: [P]ierces the senses with Oscar-worthy stylization and performances while opening the eyes to a clarity of thought about the world around us.
reviews.author: Debbie Lynn Elias

reviews.text: It was the end of times, it was the worst of times, and one of the best of times you'll have in the theater this year.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: I'm not saying that the impoverished are going to grab axes and violently murder the wealthy elite. But I'm also not NOT saying that...
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Snowpiercer has action, heart, a sense of humor, and a powerful message. The cast is talented and diverse. (...) It's the kind of genre movie the world needs more of.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: A totally unique, delightfully weird romp that offers a spark of imagination that is sorely lacking in so many of our summer movies.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Snowpiercer may not be the masterpiece that people were hoping for, but that shouldn't take away from the fact that it's a hell of a fun ride.
reviews.author: C.J. Prince

reviews.text: While not quite the artistic masterpiece that fans of the post-apocalyptic have been hailing it, Snowpiercer is still a thrilling, intriguing, blackly humorous and sometimes horrifying ride through the best and worst that humanity has to offer.
reviews.author: Iain McNally

reviews.text: By the time the end is upon you, and the twists are revealing themselves like falling dominos, it is hard to catch a breath.
reviews.author: Emmet Asher-Perrin

reviews.text: Convolution is preferable in an age where repetition and over-expository presentation is king.
reviews.author: Tara Judah

reviews.text: It's simply one of the best science fiction films in recent memory, and (thankfully) one that is completely and totally human...and often disturbingly prescient.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: The echoes of Brazil can clearly be heard in this picture along with plenty of other obvious influences, but it has enough it can call its own to be certainly worth a look.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is exactly what action fans have been clamoring for, so seek Evans & Company out and prepare yourself for a unique cinematic experience tremendously needed in this summer already full of retreads.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: The right ticket to spend on is the one that will get you onto a train, this train. All aboard!
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: The train sets make for stunning, compact, ingenious fight scenes, and one particular action sequence was so unsettling I was cringing in my seat.
reviews.author: Molly Templeton

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is an astonishingly good movie.
reviews.author: Marcianne Miller

reviews.text: What truly bowled me over was the way the first-rate cast handles the film's cumulative metaphorical weight. Evans, in particular, displays a heretofore unseen level of nuance that should silence his naysayers.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: The visuals in the film are absolutely stunning.
reviews.author: Deirdre Crimmins

reviews.text: What makes Snowpiercer a great film in my estimation is the disturbing weirdness that bleeds throughout.
reviews.author: William Evans

reviews.text: If you like your action movies beautiful, insane and a little haunting, then Snowpiercer is definitely one of the year's most essential films.
reviews.author: Charlie Jane Anders

reviews.text: "Snowpiercer" would clearly like to be the contemporary equivalent of Aldous Huxley's novel "Brave New World," but it's closer to a better-directed version of Neill Blonkamp's sci-fi dud from last year, "Elysium."
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: There's so much to love in Snowpiercer...
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Violence always involves moral questions, and the decision whether to take up armed struggle lies at the heart of revolutionary movements, but the film does not take these concerns at all seriously.
reviews.author: Anwen Crawford

reviews.text: The film is adapted from a three-volume French graphic novel, Le Transperceneige, originally published in the 1980s. Set in the aftermath of global environmental collapse, the comic is the perfect vehicle for filmmaker Bong [Joon-Ho].
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is filled to the brim with plot, characters, and action.
reviews.author: Kathy Fennessy

reviews.text: It is so rare that something lives up to expectations that it can feel like a goddamn miracle. Ladies and gentleman, I give you Bong Joon-ho's Snowpiercer.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is a fantastic dumb movie for smart people.
reviews.author: Lisa Rosman

reviews.text: One could question the movie's simplistic approach or its coolly spasmodic violence. Does it add up to anything we don't already know? Of course not. But in this case, it's absolutely the journey that matters, not the destination.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: A madcap addition to the comic-book-derived movies that have dominated cinematic summer fare.
reviews.author: J. Hoberman

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is a great entry into the sci-fi canon and one of the best films released in 2014.
reviews.author: Jay Ledbetter

reviews.text: That rare experience you don't get to have much in the summer anymore, a loud, clanging, original action flick that's grabbing you by the lapels and yelling in your ears.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Every once in a while I see a movie that leaves me vibrating with energy as I leave the theater, knowing that what I just saw will stick with me probably for the rest of my life... Snowpiercer is one of those.
reviews.author: Rebecca Pahle

reviews.text: The film's something of a mess, trading swerve and style for cohesion and coherence. No matter: Nothing else at the multiplex right now is half as entertaining.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is so didactic it will give intellectually sophisticated viewers a headache.
reviews.author: Joe Bendel

reviews.text: This is a story of class war, manifest literally and symbolically at the same time. But as he did in The Host, Bong slips his social commentary under the genre playbook.
reviews.author: Kong Rithdee

reviews.text: South Korean filmmaker Joon-ho Bong's latest is a welcome reminder of [sci-fi's] fertile - if often untilled - creative ground.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Bong's latest is his most visceral and action-oriented film to date, tapping into the generous fantasy of its stylized source material.
reviews.author: Nathan Bartlebaugh

reviews.text: Stylishly crafted while still paying attention to character development and moving the narrative forward, Snowpiercer is as good an action movie as it is an allegory about class, power structures and power run amok.
reviews.author: Theresa Smith

reviews.text: With Snowpiercer, Joon-ho demonstrates just how to make a boldly inventive modern sci-fi film without giving a damn as to what Hollywood thinks a blockbuster film should be.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: A movie that sets ground between an action movie and a reflective film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Ayala Blanco

reviews.text: Keeps all the elements of social commentary in sci-fi, but it also adds some great action sequences that could only come from the mind of its visionary director, Bong Joon-ho. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alonso Díaz de la Vega

reviews.text: This might be the best sci-fi film of the year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Ruiz

reviews.text: Proof that you can make awesome sci-fi and at the same time stimulate the brains of your audience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: The movie itself takes a lot from the action genre and moves along like the train is sets in, restlessly. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: A very smart film with many layers of reading, it's deep and entertaining at the same time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Edgardo Reséndiz

reviews.text: A smart film that keeps the suspense high at all times and works on different levels. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Eduardo Molina

reviews.text: An entertaning and thrilling film that has more substance than most recent blockbusters. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernando Santoyo Tello

reviews.text: An instant classic that you can't miss. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gonzalo Lira Galván

reviews.text: A high adrenaline dose that will make the public reflect on social and moral issues while also being amazed by and exceptional cast and fast action. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López Velarde Santibáñez

reviews.text: Manages to capture the sci-fi spirit of humanity loosing the battle against itself, not by war, just by human nature. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: "Snowpiercer" is an excellent movie that's totally worth paying to see. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandra Alarcón Cervantes

reviews.text: An unsettling and cruel vision of a terrifying near future. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: This is a new Sci-fi classic with universal appeal and endless possibilities for analysis that will have people talking for years to come. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: Bong's Snowpiercer rebels against the norms of summer blockbusters -- overthrowing them all.
reviews.author: Justin Gerber

reviews.text: Emprega seu preciosismo tcnico para construir uma alegoria cortante sobre a luta de classes.
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: It is a thing of pure cinematic beauty, the movie you want in your deck when arguing for the artistic potential of action films.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: It's brawny, ballsy and cheerfully subversive. Howard Zinn meets The Road Warrior.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The political allegory would be ham-handed indeed if it were being served up in a more serious context, but the film's zany pulp approach means Bong can get away with the baldness of the metaphor. Who needs plausibility anyway?
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Overall, this is a solid, distinctive and sometimes exquisitely inspired thriller-and-beyond.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: It's a wicked, violent parable, and one of the only movies of the summer worth talking about after the credits roll.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: It's literally a hell of a ride -- Brazil meets Murder on the Orient Express.
reviews.author: Sky Staff

reviews.text: A cool summer movie full of action, suspense, moral ambiguities, cryptic clues and villains who just won't die.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: I enjoyed every bonkers, goofy, cartoonish, creative moment of Snowpiercer.
reviews.author: Liam Maguren

reviews.text: It's the most inventive science-fiction picture in years, the most original action film in a decade and perhaps the most all-around entertaining movie so far this year.
reviews.author: AP Kryza

reviews.text: There's no easy way to pigeonhole this English-language movie from Korean writer-director Joon-ho Bong, except to say that it's a true original.
reviews.author: Ed Symkus

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is a compelling, unsettling thrill ride that's well worth the wait.
reviews.author: Genevieve Valentine

reviews.text: "Snowpiercer" warms the heart, but doesn't penetrate it.
reviews.author: Inkoo Kang

reviews.text: In just one scene of Snowpiercer, [Chris Evans] gets to act more than in all his Captain America films combined.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Fueled by implausibility, and for a good portion of the ride much better for it, Bong-Joon Ho's Snowpiercer posits a nonstop, Earth-encircling train containing the microcosmic survivors of a society killed off by a global warming-induced deep freeze.
reviews.author: Scott Marks

reviews.text: The setup may be high-concept times a thousand, but the obviousness of the symbolism is so inextricably interwoven with the forward momentum of the plot and so well complemented by Joon-ho's comic-book style and sick humor, you can't help but buy in.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: Bong Joon-ho's movie is a gripping, thrilling, utterly credible adventure.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Snowpiercer's ultimate victory is how palatable it makes its unbelievably weird material.
reviews.author: Michael Arbeiter

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is an engaging experience and is not only the most assured and interesting film of the recent Korean new-wavers' Hollywood output, but it's also a riveting action blockbuster in itself, the best of the American summer thus far.
reviews.author: Thomas Derwin

reviews.text: In a world full of Divergents and Hunger Games and 2012s, Snowpiercer not only has the confidence to ask difficult questions -- it also has the courage make the viewer answer them for his or herself.
reviews.author: Jackson Cuidon

reviews.text: This is a dark, but deeply beautiful movie, punctuated by edge-of-your-seat thrills and unexpected laughs.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Once Mr. Bong sets his monorail in motion the movie assumes an irresistible momentum, accelerated by nonstop mayhem, gallows humor and an immersive visual style that possesses a heady sense of the steam-punk Apocalypse.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: This is powerful stuff, and all the more so for its straightforwardness.
reviews.author: John Semley

reviews.text: This dystopian fantasy is unpleasant enough and inhuman enough that I never want to see it again, but it is interesting visually. The acting is also very good. Octavia Spencer ("The Help") gives a knockout performance as a desperate mother.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: A wild, weird dystopian journey that demands to be seen
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A refreshingly smart thriller, its geopolitical savvy mingled with a wholly unique look, Snowpiercer is quite the dystopian choo-choo.
reviews.author: Kimberly Gadette

reviews.text: ...a bloody, limb-severing action film with a bitterly malevolent view of the species.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: There's a righteous savagery to this movie that's almost but not quite obscured by the lushness of its imagined world.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is bonkers in the absolute best way possible.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: Given to snarling fits of action, poetic ponderings, and idiosyncratic rumblings. No action-thriller but a dystopian, steampunky class parable for a world careening towards eco-disaster . . . and so the film goes, jarring or lulling or gloriously gonzo.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: As it circumnavigates the frozen globe of the climatic post-apocalypse, 'Snowpiercer' sometimes seems loaded with more allegorical freight than even a futuristic bullet train can carry. Yet it remains one of the year's more impressive films.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Snowpiercer wears its inspirations on its sleeve, but the cumulative effect of it all results in something truly unique. It may not be The Host, but it is something I've never seen before, and that is a treat in itself.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: An environmental, post-apocalyptic, revolutionary-uprising sci-fi action movie on a train. Sub-genres don't come much more specific than Snowpiercer.
reviews.author: Tim Martain

reviews.text: It is the most frigid movie to come along since Dr. Zhivago.
reviews.author: Mal Vincent

reviews.text: Best enjoyed as a thriller on steel wheels with a salutary moral, Snowpiercer is cinematic and compelling, despite its flaws, which emerge on too close a scrutiny of the screenplay, which tried hard to be original, but is caught up in its own story cogs
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: The bold cinematic style of Boon Joon-ho strikes gold in this striking and powerful drama in which control and the order of things are key
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: A mastery of form and commentary.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: a taut social allegory about class and power cleverly packaged as an exhilarating action thriller
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Although it is based on the French graphic novel Le Transperceneige ... Snowpiercer is the best video game movie ever made.
reviews.author: Stephen Danay

reviews.text: This is Snowpiercer, one of the most uniquely fascinating, exciting, and disturbing science fiction films to come along in a good while.
reviews.author: Mark Hughes

reviews.text: It's very much part of a cinematic tradition: heir to the hermetically enclosed, purpose-built steampunk dystopias devised by Terry Gilliam and Guillermo del Toro and Caro & Jeunet.
reviews.author: Shane Danielsen

reviews.text: Loftily pretentious, though curiously amusing arthouse action movie.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: It is far from flawless -- there are too many longeurs and lapses of logic that impeded its progress along the way -- but it is alive with ideas and imagination which see it across the occasional piece of imperfect track.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: The world has ended in film after film in recent years, but rarely has the aftermath been such impressive viewing.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: Often inspired, sometimes lethargic adaption of a French graphic novel, funded mainly by the Korean government and starring a panoply of British thespians and [Captain America himself]. An awesome 90 minute movie lurks within these very bloated 126.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: With a sharp international ensemble cast and a visually ambitious scope, the result is both exhilarating and exhausting.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Snowpiercer alternates between sudden violence, high camp, and heavy-handed political allegory with breakneck speed, and even when its disjoined plot mechanics seem a little too convenient, it's brimming with new cinematic technique.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: At the dramatic center of SNOWPIERCER is this metaphorical concept of balance. We're taken on a journey to the front of a futuristic train, learning about an ecosystem that travels roughly over icy tracks. It's a ride worth taking.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The undisputed star of the show... is Korean director Boon Jong-Ho. Rarely does a vision so ambitious and raw hit the screen with such clarity and force.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: No question I would recommend it and people have got to see it on the big screen.
reviews.author: Judith Lucy

reviews.text: This is a beautifully made science fiction allegory about the perversions and arrogance of power.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: It's so hard to describe how amazing Snowpiercer is without giving away everything that makes it amazing.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: A thought provoking science fiction masterpiece...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: A confronting think piece wrapped in a bizarre and bloody thrill ride.
reviews.author: Tom Clift

reviews.text: The absolutely watchable vibe comes to an almost dead stop as the movie enters its anti-climactic third act...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: One of the biggest problems is the train setting. We're supposed to be in constant motion, but half the shots are entirely still.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: It's stylish and smart -- a big, honking metaphor, yes, but an effective one and a relevant one.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: You couldn't ask for a better metaphor for hell on Earth than what Bong Joon-ho has wrought with Snowpiercer: constant forward momentum while getting absolutely nowhere, suffering all the while.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Snowpiercer features uneven performances, but gets great mileage from its set design, the sheer audacity of the premise, and the appearance of one of those movie villains who seem able to take lethal punishment without actually dying.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Snowpiercer feels both heightened and grounded, allegorical yet familiar, able to be experienced. The confined space in no way inhibits tension or excitement, or a sense of forward momentum. It's a film not to be missed.
reviews.author: Philippa Hawker

reviews.text: Suddenly zombies, nukes or a global pandemic don't seem nearly as devastating as a train ride to nowhere.
reviews.author: Lori Hoffman

reviews.text: A movie-movie, with edgy cred and a vivid dystopian vision that, while ostensibly futuristic, speaks harshly to the class divide already defining us.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Every moment of genius and every half-formed lump alike make this one of the completely essential films of the year.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Merits near-hyperbolic praise.
reviews.author: Rob Humanick

reviews.text: Violent, often absurd, but full of brilliant surprises.
reviews.author: David Denby

reviews.text: It emerges from a place of fearsome ambition, dressed in the skin of a zealous summer blockbuster but equipped with a brain that far exceeds the standards of its classification.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: Snowpiercer hits the sweet spot of working as entertainment while still having enough brains to keep you intellectually engaged. It's a movie for people who love movies that play by their own rules.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The provocative film is one big metaphor for the chaos in present-day society, divided along class-lines.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A film full of both wonders and horrors, rendered beautifully and hugely.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Few of the screenplay's class-struggle elements are new, and they are driven home in some scenes with a very heavy hand. However, the cast, visual conceptualization, production design and art direction are so strong that these criticisms are fairly minor.
reviews.author: Fr. Chris Carpenter

reviews.text: ...the film becomes a horrifying, social commentary that bites close to the bone.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Hauntingly grim, full of appalling ironies and awful truths. This is most definitely not the feel-good movie of the summer.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: In a word, 'Wow!' Bong Joon-ho's Snowpiercer, is near the very top of 2014′s "Best of" list -- at least so far, and I can't imagine it slipping out of the top five.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is a rare movie that respects the audience's intelligence, subtly mining Titanic (in a good way), The Wizard of Oz, and Runaway Train for tropes.
reviews.author: Gary Dowell

reviews.text: The element of surprise is the most effective weapon in Joon-ho's directorial arsenal.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: One of the few surprises of the Summer and one that deserves a much wider audience.
reviews.author: Scott Nash

reviews.text: Utterly surreal and completely mental.
reviews.author: Widgett Walls

reviews.text: The future is miserably dystopian as usual in this apocalyptic sci-fi thriller, but at least it's thoughtful, stylishly crafted, high-speed misery that keeps on hurtling relentlessly forward -- even though there's nowhere to go.
reviews.author: Bruce Ingram

reviews.text: Within the space of a 60-foot-by-9-foot train car, "Snowpiercer" packs in more action, inventiveness, energy and ideas than most summer blockbusters that have whole galaxies at their disposal.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: ...has about it a gorgeous incoherency that overwhelms any logical objections to its absurd premise.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: It pummels forward like the train on which the action is set, and you don't particularly want to reach the end.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: An object of blunt force and breath-catching beauty, Snowpiercer plays what-if with a familiar doomsday scenario: What if Noah's ark never found dry land again?
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: It's a downbeat spectacle. But very good, unforgettably bizarre, original filmmaking and adventurously explored ideas can leave you feeling high, especially when you don't know quite how it's been pulled off.
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: It's a bleak, shocker of a movie, but one laced with just enough black humor to make the harsher parts even bleaker.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: As with The Host, the political satire is teased out gradually as the story progresses and never intrudes on one's enjoyment of the movie's richly imagined world.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: Besides the impressive visuals, the film makes relatively solid use of its impressive cast.
reviews.author: Mark Rozeman

reviews.text: If you can buy the premise of this Bong Joon-ho graphic novel adaptation, you're in for a good ride.
reviews.author: Joe Lozito

reviews.text: ...the kind of taut action sci-fi thriller that it really needs to be seen on a big screen to get the full experience.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: You could reduce the narrative elements to Das Boot meets Metropolis, but that's saying too much and too little. Cinematic intelligence and Bong's unwavering class-consciousness offer up a fierce fable for our end times.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: The Taking of Swinton One Two Three.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Exciting, edge-of-your-seat action thriller - a wild ride that's one of the best of the year, so far.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: It's a dumb idea on its surface, and as we get deeper and deeper into the concept, at no point does the screenplay ... make us believe it is anything more than that.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: "Snowpiercer" delivers tension, and surprises in ways that belie the conventional wisdom that blockbuster action movies must be brainless, soulless enterprises.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The political message of Snowpiercer is delivered without much finesse, but Bong succeeds in other ways.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: A messy bit of inspired madness. I love a film that's just shy of feeling like it could've been a suicide note.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Bong's top priority is to deliver a meaty, satisfying action adventure, and he succeeds there like the world-class filmmaker he is.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: In the thick of summer, while Hollywood is busy cranking out cookie-cutter superhero movies and giant robot sequels, along comes Snowpiercer to show everyone how it's done.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: Although there is plenty to think about here, it's best not to overthink it. Just hang on and enjoy the ride.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: "Snowpiercer" is a rich, ravishing experience, a motion picture dripping in social consciousness and thematic intricacy without becoming preachy or losing sight of its other purpose as a rousing, robust entertainment.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: "Snowpiercer" is a welcome curiosity in a season of formula-driven, copycat genre films.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: The dystopian world he envisions is incredibly immersive and extremely thrilling....but maybe some of those edits should have been kept in.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Most excellent action movie, social commentary and survival saga (among other things).
reviews.author: Clint O'Connor

reviews.text: Rich in theme and artistry, Snowpiercer is spellbinding, offering those hungry for big screen anarchy a story that actually provides stakes, causalities, and a paralyzing sting of remorse.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: For just about everything maniacally cool in the movie, there's a flaw, sometimes a near-fatal one.
reviews.author: Marc Mohan

reviews.text: A formidable, if perversely overlong epic, Snowpiercer is a dystopian moral parable about survivors of a second ice age that wipes out virtually all humanity.
reviews.author: Tirdad Derakhshani

reviews.text: This is brilliant, bizarre, fearless filmmaking.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: The production design is sharp and unique, though the movie itself is not without its flaws.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: The movie never stops moving, and its conclusion is one of the most bittersweet-yet still somehow victorious-endings of any big-budget action movie I can remember.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: In different hands, Snowpiercer might have been just another generic action movie. Yet with South Korean director Bong Joon-ho at the helm, it's instead something more off-kilter and more disturbingly satisfying.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Subtlety may not be the film's strong suit, but it creates a richly imagined world, as glitteringly arresting as it is savagely merciless.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: It may not be the brightest movie around, but it's almost insanely watchable...deliciously different from run-of-the-mill doomsday pictures.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Impressive and pretty amazing. This is how you make a film.
reviews.author: Chase Whale

reviews.text: But with a game supporting cast including Ewan Bremner and Octavia Spencer, well-paced direction, superb cinematography, plus a gripping adventure story to boot, Snowpiercer rolls along at super speed, making any complaining seem like nitpicking.
reviews.author: Brandon Judell

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is one of those rare modern action movies that keeps the audience guessing...it's packed with fascinating ideas and presents a fully fleshed-out universe.
reviews.author: Sherilyn Connelly

reviews.text: An incendiary agitprop scifi masterpiece.
reviews.author: Devin Faraci

reviews.text: a masterpiece of action adventure science fiction fueled by a terrific international cast...Joon-ho has more on his mind than startling imagery and violence and his climax is both breathtaking and an emotional gut punch.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The best action film of 2014, and probably the best film, period.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: A unique vision, strong execution (in action, wit, and humor) as well as compelling characters culminate in one of the year's best dark horse hits.
reviews.author: Kofi Outlaw

reviews.text: Something truly special, a unique and bracing science-fiction film that stirs both heart and mind.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: [It] seems to have been sent back to us from some distant alternate future where grandiose summer action movies can also be lovingly crafted, thematically ambitious works of art.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: An unprecedented combination of stunning combat, stylistic eccentricities and dramatic poignancy that is so rich and enthralling, there's no way one viewing will ever be enough.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: SNOWPIERCER is a big film with a large cast, but Bong brilliantly juggles fights, characters, and ideas -- including a savvy use of food -- and fits it all succinctly within his amazing visual design and scope.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: From a dramatic standpoint, the film is equally effective in the way that it includes the expected pulpy thrills and weirdo humor but also some unexpectedly affecting dramatic moments.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Now, at last, comes a fun dystopian sci-fi epic - a splattery shambles with a fat dose of social satire and barely a lick of sense.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: The movie is baldly schematic, and largely grim and grubby. It wears you down.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Easily one of the best science fiction films of the year.
reviews.author: Rob Vaux

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is a rare hybrid that perfectly blends the dazzle of a futuristic action thriller with the intellectual substance of an art film.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: This eccentric journey has everything more ambitious entertainment seekers crave...
reviews.author: Anna Tatarska

reviews.text: Snowpiercer balances class metaphor, a nice hunk of comic book strangeness and often-ingeniously choreographed action in equal measure.
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: In "Snowpiercer," Bong's first English-language film, nothing gets lost in translation.
reviews.author: Betsy Sharkey

reviews.text: Planetary destruction and human extinction happen a half-dozen times every summer. It's rarely this refreshing, though.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: The train, and the picture, barrel along to an apocalyptic climax that will leave you shaken and chilled.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: This is a terrific, dark dystopian nightmare mixed with flashes of Terry Gilliam-esque absurdity and the filmmaker's own fractured frame of reference.
reviews.author: Bill Gibron

reviews.text: This is exactly the sort of ambitious, audacious, and uncompromising filmmaking that deserves to be seen.
reviews.author: Ian Buckwalter

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is everything Transformers: Age of Extinction wishes it could be: a slambam sci-fi thriller with a brain, a heart and an artful sense of purpose.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Snowpiercer sucks you into its strange, brave new world so completely, it leaves you with the all-too-rare sensation that you've just witnessed something you've never seen before...and need to see again.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: [Bong Joon-ho] lays out class sideways, one section at a time, so that by the time you get to the people lounging in Jacuzzis or clubbing, it's impossible to avoid outrage.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: It's a film that, in its own peculiar way, forces viewers to question their values and ask themselves how much they're willing to sacrifice for a functioning society, and how much is too much.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A genuinely spectacular project that has the imaginative and philosophical dimensions that most blockbusters would never dream of venturing into.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: By the time "Snowpiercer" closes we've been guided through an exhilarating, videogame-fighting infographic of the post-globalization world ecosystem: climate change, child labor and population control. And it's fun, too!
reviews.author: Brian Formo

reviews.text: One of the best SF actioners we've seen in a very long time!
reviews.author: James O'Ehley

reviews.text: Like a train, Snowpiercer picks up steam as it goes, and its last half is commercial cinema at its best: thrilling, visually striking, and endlessly thought-provoking.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Though shocking violence and black humor run through the length of the movie, what comes through most strongly is its pessimistic political conscience; were the movie less earnest, it might seem Verhoeven-esque.
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: The nihilism would be cooler if it felt like more was at stake. But if you settle in, it's one wild ride.
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: Don't miss it - this is enormously fun visionary filmmaking, with a witty script and a great international cast.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: I'm not sure where the line is between a good gonzo movie and a creative mess, but I know that Snowpiercer is on the right side of it.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: A dystopian masterwork illustrating the moral rot of dividing the population into a winning class versus everybody else as poor scum of the earth.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Significantly dark, this sci-fi film is also lyrical, funny, and occasionally self-indulgent. It's a bumpy ride, but one well worth taking.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: If you love movies, you can't afford to miss it.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: The most bracing and liberating thing about Joon-ho Bong's Snowpiercer is not just its lyrical forward motion, but the exuberance with which the film revels in its plot predicament.
reviews.author: David Thomson

reviews.text: Sprung from a 1982 French graphic novel and bearing its era's trickle-down tensions, Snowpiercer is a headlong rush into conceptual lunacy-but you'll love it anyway.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: This is the kind of science-fiction film that I wish they made more of, something big and bold and unafraid to reach for greatness.
reviews.author: Drew McWeeny

reviews.text: Even as dystopian dramas go, the picture is arid and lusterless in its more serious moments and unpleasantly kitschy when it tries to soar over the top.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Excessive in an interesting way for much longer than you think it could be. Unfortunately, that's not long enough.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: Projecting the problems of today into a science-fiction tomorrow, [Snowpiercer] also ties them to a compelling story that keeps shifting under its characters' feet.
reviews.author: Keith Phipps

reviews.text: Bong brings enough straight action to the mix that even those put off by the more bizarre characters should ultimately dig what he's done with the material.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is a strange and colourful beast: messy, uneven and full of weird indulgences and dangling plot threads. But by God it's good fun.
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: In its focus both on the looming disaster of climate change and the swelling economic disparity between the rich and everyone else, it's both timely and relevant, while keeping the entertainment quotient high.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: Against all odds, though not totally unexpected given the director's previous skill with the erratic, the end result is quite spectacular.
reviews.author: Josh Slater-Williams

reviews.text: An entertainingly off-kilter slice of pulpy mainstream filmmaking, executed with humour, verve and vision.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Elaborately produced sci-fi that takes place almost completely within the last train out of anywhere.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: The film preaches resolutely to the choir, and cinephiles in sync with the film's politics may still blanch at how snugly their interests are courted.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: Echoing the dystopian brilliance of Blade Runner and Brazil and beset by remarkably similar studio wrangling over the final cut, Snowpiercer is an audacious, immersive and nightmarish masterpiece.
reviews.author: Ben Rawson-Jones

reviews.text: Snowpiercer works brilliantly, the sum of extremely disparate parts that adds up to cinematic excellence.
reviews.author: Andrew Pulver

reviews.text: Roaring action, thoughtful geekery, and a knockout performance by Chris Evans send Snowpiercer speeding out of the station and into the sci-fi history books.
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: If the film has one element that never flags or falters, it's Evans.
reviews.author: James Rocchi

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is leaden and confused, an all-star disaster of a movie, of interest only to connoisseurs of expensively botched sci-fi money-pits.
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Maybe some restraint would have improved Snowpiercer in the traditional sense, but I wouldn't want to live in that world.
reviews.author: Christopher Runyon

reviews.text: Once the action heats up, Bong delivers a rich feast of political allegory and bloodthirsty carnage. Snowpiecer is no masterpiece, but an agreeably unorthodox, impressively arty blockbuster.
reviews.author: Stephen Dalton

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is still an intellectually and artistically superior vehicle to many of the end-of-days futuristic action thrillers out there.
reviews.author: Clarence Tsui

reviews.text: The world building, the provocative concept and the thrilling adventure are everything I want in a movie.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Unapologetically long and messy, Snowpiercer offers an unhinged ride that's worth the investment for its mixture of batty personalities, consistently impressive visuals and mad swipes at heavy symbolism jam-packed together.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: The cast is excellent, amplifying their mostly simple roles with their talents and presence.
reviews.author: Seongyong Cho

reviews.text: While the highly stylized set pieces are certainly eye catching, they start to feel disjointed and nonsensical.
reviews.author: Allison Loring

reviews.text: A crazy, blood- and action-soaked piece of bravura filmmaking.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: ...a fairy tale of sorts with darker motives, more violence than the Grimms would envision, and some nasty things to say about libertarianism versus control.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: A fantastic achievement: a novel, passionate, and energized sci-fi with wild action and strange humor.
reviews.author: Scott Weinberg

reviews.text: Snowpiercer is an ambitious and stylishly designed slice of dystopian sci-fi, yet it is also incomplete, filled with shallow characters and unexplored ideas.
reviews.author: Jordan Adler

reviews.text: Chris Evans takes charge on this truth as strange as science fiction express to nowhere, as a deprived but dashing commuter warrior on wheels. While facing off against a terror tycoon's lookalike dead ringers for the menacing hooded neo-nazis of Kiev.
reviews.author: Prairie Miller

reviews.text: Though completely absurd in many ways, Bong's handling of the source material is so expertly done that we're completely immersed in this tale, allowing for ourselves to be taken wherever the South Korean director sees fit.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: ...a visionary, thrilling work...a crystallization of Bong's status as one of our most exciting filmmakers, and to alter it would be something close to vandalism.
reviews.author: Oliver Lyttelton

reviews.text: An enthralling ride that never runs out of momentum as it cleverly examines the issue of social class in a thoroughly engaging, yet complex manner.
reviews.author: Jason Bechervaise

reviews.text: An enormously ambitious, visually stunning and richly satisfying futuristic epic from the gifted Korean genre director Bong Joon-ho.
reviews.author: Scott Foundas

synopsis: A post-apocalyptic ice age forces humanity's last survivors aboard a globe-spanning supertrain. One man (Chris Evans) will risk everything to lead a revolt for control of the engine and the future of the world.
